title: Twenty Goals. Thirty-Nine Years Old. Messi Faces Salah in Atlanta With a Quarterfinal Spot on the Line.
excerpt: The final day of the World Cup's Round of 16 brings the tournament's biggest showdown yet — and completes the quarterfinal bracket that stretches from Foxborough to Miami.
body:
Key Takeaways
  • Messi has scored 20 World Cup goals, the most in history.
  • Salah leads Egypt into their first knockout win since 1934.
  • Argentina relies heavily on Messi, who scored seven of their 11 goals.
  • Quarterfinals feature high-stakes matches, including Argentina vs Egypt.
  • India's diaspora is engaged, with 300 million viewers for football.

The FIFA World Cup's Round of 16 concludes on Tuesday in North America, and the final day has saved its headliner for last. Lionel Messi's Argentina face Mohamed Salah's Egypt at Mercedes-Benz Stadium in Atlanta at noon ET, with the last quarterfinal spot on the bracket's upper half hanging in the balance. Then it's Switzerland against Colombia at BC Place in Vancouver at 4 PM ET. When the dust settles, the eight-team quarterfinal field — and the road to the July 19 final at MetLife Stadium — will be complete. ## Messi's Record-Breaking Run The numbers have entered absurd territory. At 39, Messi has scored seven goals in four matches at this World Cup, extending his record of scoring in seven consecutive World Cup games. His tournament tally now stands at **20 career World Cup goals** — more than any player in history, surpassing both Miroslav Klose (16) and Cristiano Ronaldo (who was sent home Monday when Spain eliminated Portugal 1-0 in Arlington). ![Mohamed Salah — Photo: Wikimedia Commons](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/4/4a/Mohamed_Salah_2018.jpg) He is tied with Kylian Mbappé and Erling Haaland for the Golden Boot, each with seven goals. But it is the nature of Argentina's dependence on Messi that should give the defending champions pause. He has scored seven of their 11 tournament goals. When he hasn't scored, Argentina has looked vulnerable — they needed extra time to escape Cape Verde 3-2 in the Round of 32, with an own goal in the 111th minute sparing their blushes. ## Salah's Last Dance > **"The "last dance" narrative has threaded through the entire tournament, but on Tuesday in Atlanta, it collides head-on."** Egypt, meanwhile, are making history simply by being here. Their penalty-shootout victory over Australia in the Round of 32 was their first knockout-round win at a World Cup since 1934 — a 92-year gap that makes this run feel almost mythical. Mohamed Salah, 34, delivered a composed panenka in that shootout, and while his tournament stats are modest (one goal, two assists), his presence transforms Egypt from plucky underdogs into genuine danger. He will know that Argentina's defense showed cracks against Cape Verde — and a player who has tormented the best defenders in the Premier League for nearly a decade won't need a second invitation. ![Miroslav Klose — Photo: Wikimedia Commons](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/8/8c/2016209185719_2016-07-27_Champions_for_Charity_-_Sven_-_1D_X_-_0149_-_DV3P4742_mod.jpg) This is almost certainly Salah's last World Cup. It is almost certainly Messi's, too. The "last dance" narrative has threaded through the entire tournament, but on Tuesday in Atlanta, it collides head-on. ## Switzerland vs Colombia: The Dark Horse Clash The later kickoff in Vancouver is the kind of match that decides World Cups without anyone noticing until the semifinal. Colombia, who beat Ghana 1-0 in the Round of 32 after finishing runners-up to Portugal in Group K, have been steady rather than spectacular. Switzerland, who dispatched Algeria 2-0, have been similarly efficient. The winner faces either Argentina or Egypt in the quarterfinal on Saturday at Arrowhead Stadium in Kansas City.

![Cristiano Ronaldo — Photo: Wikimedia Commons](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/6/67/Cristiano_Ronaldo_2275_%28cropped%29.jpg) ## The Quarterfinal Bracket Six of eight quarterfinal spots are already locked in after yesterday's dramatic double-header that saw Belgium demolish the USA 4-1 in Seattle and Spain edge Portugal in Arlington: - **Thursday, July 9** — France vs Morocco, 4 PM ET, Gillette Stadium, Foxborough, MA - **Friday, July 10** — Spain vs Belgium, 3 PM ET, SoFi Stadium, Inglewood, CA - **Saturday, July 11** — Norway vs England, 5 PM ET, Hard Rock Stadium, Miami, FL - **Saturday, July 11** — (Argentina/Egypt winner) vs (Switzerland/Colombia winner), 9 PM ET, Arrowhead Stadium, Kansas City, MO The quarterfinals carry their own blockbuster storylines. France-Morocco is a rematch of the 2022 semifinal. Spain face a Belgium side that just humiliated the host nation. And Norway's Erling Haaland — fresh off ending Neymar's World Cup career with a brace in New Jersey — goes up against England, who survived Mexico 3-2 in Mexico City. ## Why NRIs Are Watching India may not have qualified for the World Cup, but the tournament has never been more accessible to the diaspora. Every remaining match is being played on North American soil — in cities where Indian communities are deeply rooted. Atlanta, which hosts Tuesday's headline act, has one of the fastest-growing Indian-American populations in the country. Vancouver, Los Angeles, Miami, Kansas City, and Foxborough are all within driving distance or a short flight for millions of NRIs.

Football is India's second-most-watched sport, with an estimated 300 million viewers. Messi, in particular, commands a massive following in India that stretches back to his first World Cup in 2006. For diaspora fans who grew up watching him in Kolkata living rooms and are now watching him in American stadiums, this might be the last time. **Where to watch**: Fox, Telemundo, Peacock (streaming), and Fubo. Argentina vs Egypt kicks off at 9 AM PT / noon ET. Switzerland vs Colombia follows at 1 PM PT / 4 PM ET.
